To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) it is possible to train a statistical MT system to translate components of a compound in contiguous positions; (ii) it is possible for a system to translate the correct order of components of a compound, even if the components are split in the training data; and (iii) a learning-based method for compound merging can produce novel compounds that are not in the training data.

the method for generating compounds in statistical machine translation is better when the components are translated in contiguous positions, and when they are translated in the right order; that this method can be improved by merging components that are in consecutive positions, and that the best method for this task is a learning-based method.

(i) we propose a new approach for increasing the chances of producing contiguous components in the output; (ii) we propose new methods for compound merging that outperform all the existing methods; and (iii) we propose a learning-based method for compound merging that has similar accuracy than the heuristic method, but is better at producing new compounds.
